_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for The Indian Hotels Company (consolidated, Rs crore). Built by reported segment: Hotels (room, F&B, other operating income and management fees, kept in businessLines.hotel and checked against the segment in INDHOTEL.ctx.js), Air catering (TajSATS, 51%) and the inter-segment elimination. Group operating EBITDA = sum of segments (post-Ind AS 116, as reported; other income below EBITDA). Minorities and associates have no line in the engine: they sit in the tax rate (see _taxWhy) and in the SOTP.

segments.name: Hotels
segments._why: Sum of the four streams in businessLines.hotel: room revenue +14.5% / +11% / +10% (like-for-like RevPAR +7-9% a year, management's range, plus ~800 leased/owned keys in FY27 incl. Frankfurt, ANK/Pride, Atmantan and Brij for a full year; Q1FY27 room +16%), F&B +9.5% / +8.5% / +8% (Q1 +9%; weddings and MICE), other operating income +28% / +14% / +12% (Atmantan consolidated from 16-Jan-2026; Q1 +49%), management fees +19% / +18% / +17% (Q1 +26%; guide high-teens; 26,250 managed keys in the pipeline). FY27 +14.3% sits at the top of the 12-14% consolidated guide because air catering grows slower.
segments._marginWhy: Operating EBITDA margin FY25 34.0%, FY26 34.3%, Q1FY27 30.1% (+1.1 pp YoY despite ~Rs12-15 cr of Frankfurt and Noida start-up costs; Q1 is the seasonally weakest quarter). 35.0% / 35.6% / 36.0%: operating leverage on like-for-like rate growth and a rising fee share (fees are ~80% margin), partly offset by leased hotels (license fees) and lower-margin acquisitions.

segments.name: Air catering (TajSATS, 51%)
segments._why: FY26 Rs1,210 cr (+17%, partly the full-year effect of consolidation from Aug-2024); Q1FY27 +3% as West Asia flight cuts hit international meals. +7% in FY27 (recovery from H2, management: 'three to six months' from double digits), then +12% with the Noida kitchen and airport traffic growth.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 23.7% (airport levy pass-through cost ~1-2 pp), Q1FY27 19.5% with Noida kitchen start-up costs. 21.5% / 23.0% / 23.5%.

segments.name: Inter-segment elimination
segments._why: TajSATS meals sold to IHCL hotels; FY26 -Rs8 cr. Engine has no elimination line, so it is a negative segment with zero margin.

_unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in any segment
_unallocWhy: Segments sum to consolidated operating EBITDA as reported (FY26 Rs2,907 + Rs287 = Rs3,194 cr vs Rs3,195 cr; Screener Rs3,196 cr).

businessLines._why: Hotel segment build (Rs cr). FY26 base: room 4,283, F&B 2,829, other operating income 690, management fees 685 = 8,487 (Q4FY26 deck slide 45). Growth per stream in segments[0]._why.

_capexWhy: Cash capex guide Rs1,100-1,300 cr for FY27 and Rs1,000-1,200 cr a year after (renovations, greenfield on-balance-sheet keys: Bandstand, Shiroda, Lakshadweep, Ginger Goa Mopa, Bengaluru airport) plus ~Rs100-150 cr a year of new leases (right-of-use; Frankfurt in FY27), because the model's net cash deducts lease liabilities. FY26 capex Rs1,037 cr, FY25 Rs1,074 cr. Brij (Rs222 cr, Apr-2026) is not in capex; it is in the net cash bridge in the valuation chapter.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs605 cr = 3.8% of average gross block (Rs15,911 cr incl. right-of-use); Q1FY27 Rs163 cr (Rs652 cr annualised). 3.8% gives FY27E ~Rs670 cr with Frankfurt.
_treasuryWhy: Zero: the engine would apply it to net cash after lease liabilities. Treasury income is built on gross cash in otherIncome.
_otherIncomeWhy: Built from AR FY26 consolidated note 25 (Rs282 cr): treasury Rs219 cr (bank interest Rs93 cr + mutual-fund gains Rs126 cr) on ~Rs3,700 cr average gross cash = ~5.9%; dividends on equity investments Rs33 cr; other Rs30 cr. FY27E: ~6% on ~Rs4,700 cr average gross cash (Rs4,439 cr at Jun-26) = ~Rs280 cr + dividends ~Rs35 cr + other ~Rs15 cr = Rs330 cr (Q1FY27 Rs80 cr x 4 = Rs320 cr). Then +Rs30 cr a year as cash builds. Excludes exceptional items (Screener's FY26 Rs557 cr includes Rs309 cr of them) and the share of associates (in the tax rate).
_interestWhy: FY26 Rs221 cr with gross bank debt of only Rs51 cr: it is almost all interest on Rs2,786 cr of lease liabilities. Q1FY27 Rs57 cr (Rs228 cr annualised); Frankfurt lease from Jun-2026 adds ~Rs10 cr.
_taxWhy: Tax plus minorities less associates (engine workaround: no minority or associate line). FY26 before exceptional items: PBT Rs2,650 cr, PAT before minorities and associates Rs1,960 cr (tax 26.0%), associates + minorities -Rs111 cr, attributable PAT Rs1,849 cr = 30.2% leakage. Q1FY27: PBT Rs533 cr to Rs358 cr = 32.8% (associates nil). 31%: tax ~25.5% + minorities ~6.5% of PBT (TajSATS 49%, PIEM 41%, Benares 48%, St James 20%, ANK/Pride/Atmantan/Brij 49%) less associates ~1%.
_payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs3.25 a share (incl. a special Rs0.50) = 22% of reported EPS; Rs2.75 ordinary = 21% of EPS before exceptional items. 20%.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash after lease liabilities, so the 12.2% cost of equity is also the WACC; beta 0.95: travel demand is cyclical (Covid, West Asia) but IHCL has no financial leverage.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian travel and hotel spending grows with nominal GDP; 6% nominal, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10-11% to 8% by year 15 as like-for-like rate growth normalises and the managed pipeline matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 34%: hotel margins ~36% diluted by TajSATS (~23%) and leased hotels; FY26 33.0%.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades from ~11% of revenue to 8% (renovation ~5% plus growth keys); FY26 10.7%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: West Asia normalises by H2FY27, like-for-like RevPAR grows ~10% a year (Jefferies case), Frankfurt and the acquisitions ramp fast, fees compound at 20%+ and the market pays the top quartile of IHCL's own post-Covid multiple range after the same sector move.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The 2026 travel shock lingers: inbound and MICE stay weak, like-for-like RevPAR grows ~4-5%, new supply in Goa, Bengaluru and Delhi caps rates, TajSATS stays near 20% margins and hotel multiples stay at the bottom quartile after the sector de-rating.

parts.name: Hotels (owned, leased and managed)
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E hotel EBITDA (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Post-Ind AS EBITDA; lease liabilities are in the net cash line. Multiple derived in the valuation chapter.

parts.name: TajSATS: IHCL's 51% at the same multiple
parts.note: Same EV/EBITDA as hotels (ICICI Securities values TajSATS on its hotel multiple) × 51%; SATS's 49% is therefore not deducted again.

parts.name: Less: minorities in hotel subsidiaries
parts.metricLabel: 5.0% (hotel minorities ÷ hotel profit before minorities) × hotel EV
parts.note: PIEM 41.35%, Benares 48.03%, St James Court 20.33%, United Hotels / NIHL ~45%, ANK, Pride, Atmantan and Brij 49% (AR FY26 note 39). Checked in INDHOTEL.ctx.js.

parts.name: Oriental Hotels (35.86%) at market less 20%, replacing book
parts.metricLabel: 6.40 cr shares × Rs142.36 (30-Sep-2026) × 0.8 − Rs322 cr book in model cash
parts.note: Listed associate; bull 10%, bear 30% discount. The 24-Aug-2026 merger scheme (25 IHCL for 117 OHL) is shown as a sensitivity.

parts.name: Less: Brij acquisition paid after Mar-26 (not in model cash)
parts.metricLabel: Up to Rs222 cr for 51% (IHCL ~Rs127 cr, ANK ~Rs34 cr, Pride ~Rs61 cr), completed 21-Apr-2026
parts.note: Brij's EBITDA is in our hotel forecasts from FY27; its 49% minority is in the hotel minorities line.

parts.name: Net cash at Sep-28E (model: cash and investments less borrowings incl. leases)
parts.note: Mar-26: Screener cash Rs1,831 cr + investments Rs3,606 cr (incl. JVs/associates at book) − borrowings Rs2,837 cr (bank Rs51 cr + leases Rs2,786 cr) = Rs2,600 cr.

methods.name: Sum of the parts (EV/EBITDA)
methods.why: How the street values IHCL: EV/EBITDA on FY28E or Jun-28E EBITDA (ICICI Direct 29x, Axis 27x, Anand Rathi ~26x, Nomura ~23x), three as a SOTP that deducts minorities and adds Oriental Hotels and 51% of TajSATS (Motilal Oswal 28x, ICICI Securities 30x).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on attributable earnings: own forward P/E median adjusted for the sector P/E move.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, 12.2% discount rate, 6% terminal growth, plus net cash after leases.
